title: Open API answers 404 for the internal invoice by id
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Use an Open API key for the test organization, the Open API documentation, and a tool that sends API requests.
  • Make sure the Internal Work Orders setting is on in Settings > Work Orders.
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer A, flagged as an Internal customer.
  • Have a new internal work order for this test, work order 1, for internal customer A, closed, whose internal invoice id is taken from the work order's Finance tab address.
custom_steps: 1. Send GET /v1/invoices/[id] with the id of work order 1's internal invoice.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The response is 404.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.0 final (9 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11833 (Story 11, Open API and webhooks)

  • S11-R2: “A closed internal or no-charge work order returns the status closed, a new value next to the existing ones, with its classification. Its internal invoice is never listed by GET /v1/invoices, GET /v1/work-orders/{id}/invoices or GET /v1/customers/{id}/invoices, from the core release on (S3-R4), so a consumer never has to skip it, and GET /v1/invoices/{id} answers 404 for it; the work order resource carries what an integration needs. Until this story ships, the work order reads invoiced in the API. Reopen returns the work order to completed.”

From: Jira tickets under epic SV-11665 (saved 12 Nov 2026, sources/JIRA-SV-11665-tickets-2026-11-12.md), read 12 Nov 2026

  • Jira SV-11976: “The asset's Invoices tab lists the closed record at $0.00; no closed record appears on any receivables list, and the Open API answers 404 for it on `/v1/invoices/{id}`.”
